findings.passage: Senator Hyde-Smith, who holds an enhanced-carry permit, is a strong advocate for protecting the Constitutional right of law-abiding citizens to keep and bear arms. The Senator has authored and supported federal legislation defending Second Amendment rights and is committed to supporting efforts that would prevent the federal government from infringing upon those rights.
findings.note: Issue page on her Senate site, undated, in the third person (office copy).
subjects: carry a gun with a permit

findings.passage: “The Second Amendment rights of law-abiding citizens remain imperiled as Democrats and anti-gun activists lean into government overreach.  The GRIP Act is needed to clarify that states and localities cannot use federal funds or data to keep gun registries that can lead to infringing on a constitutional right,”
findings.note: Her quote in her office's release on reintroducing the GRIP Act (S.3916).

findings.motion: S.3916, Gun-owner Registration Information Protection (GRIP) Act
findings.note: Release says she and Rep. Gosar reintroduced a bill barring states and localities from using federal funds or background-check data to keep gun registries; she is its author per the April 2026 release.

findings.passage: “Our brief is part of the ongoing work to protect the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding citizens from leftist states run by anti-gun activists.  These states shouldn’t be allowed to erode the constitutional protections established by Congress by law,”
findings.note: Her quote on signing a Supreme Court friend-of-the-court brief about a New York law and the federal law shielding gun makers from suits (PLCAA).

findings.motion: Signed amicus brief to the U.S. Supreme Court supporting the NSSF petition on the Protection of Lawful Commerce in Arms Act and a New York public nuisance law
findings.note: One of 77 members of Congress who signed a brief urging the Court to overturn a Second Circuit ruling that allowed New York's law.

findings.motion: Signed letter to Acting ATF Director urging ATF to stop enforcing the vacated 2023 pistol brace rule
findings.note: Release says she signed a letter led by Sen. Cassidy. The release quotes the letter: “In our view, this since-vacated rule does not comply with the statute and cannot pass constitutional muster, and we urge ATF to cease any efforts to continue enforcing it either in substance or form,”

findings.passage: “Law-abiding citizens who want to own a firearm don’t engage in smash-and-grab robberies.  It’s the criminal element committing these crimes that leads to more illegal firearms on our streets and more crime.  It’s past time to enact this legislation to put stiffer prison sentences on the books for these criminals,”
findings.note: Her quote on the Federal Firearms Licensee Protection Act (S.4671), which raises penalties for stealing guns from licensed dealers.
subjects: tougher penalties for stealing guns from dealers

findings.motion: S.4671, Federal Firearms Licensee Protection Act (cosponsor)
findings.note: Release says she is again supporting the bill and cosponsored it in the past two Congresses; it raises penalties for stealing firearms from licensed dealers.
subjects: tougher penalties for stealing guns from dealers

findings.passage: “The right to keep and bear all firearms is a fundamental right that should not be restricted by the federal government.  This legislation would repeal the arbitrary restriction for citizens between 18 and 20 years old from purchasing a handgun,”
findings.note: Her quote on the SAME Act of 2021, a bill to let adults 18 to 20 buy a handgun from a licensed dealer.
subjects: minimum age to buy a gun

findings.motion: Second Amendment Mandates Equality (SAME) Act of 2021 (primary cosponsor)
findings.note: Release titles her a primary cosponsor of a bill to repeal the federal ban on handgun purchases from dealers by adults under 21.
subjects: minimum age to buy a gun

findings.passage: “This legislation would honor the rights of law-abiding gun owners with concealed carry permits in other states with right-to-carry laws,” Hyde-Smith said.
findings.note: Her quote on the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act (S.69).

findings.motion: S.69, Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act (original cosponsor)
findings.note: Release says she signed as an original cosponsor of a bill letting carry-permit holders carry concealed handguns across state lines.

findings.passage: “There’s no need to restrict the ability of qualified, well-trained law enforcement officers from being able to provide another level of protection for our communities. This legislation would cut through some of the unnecessary red tape involving concealed-carry rights for police officers,” Senator Hyde-Smith said.
findings.note: Her quote on the LEOSA Reform Act (S.679), page dated 2025-03-25 (a news item posted on her site).
subjects: carry a gun with a permit
carry in places where guns are barred

findings.motion: S.679, Law Enforcement Officers Safety Act (LEOSA) Reform Act (reintroduced with Sen. Kennedy)
findings.note: Page says she and Sen. Kennedy reintroduced the bill; it eases concealed-carry rules for qualified officers and retired officers, including in places where guns are barred. Date is the page date.
subjects: carry in places where guns are barred

findings.passage: “No system is infallible, including the federal bureaucracy.  The ATF Transparency Act would help ensure law-abiding Americans aren’t denied their Second Amendment rights due to mistakes in their background checks that may wrongfully prevent them from owning a firearm,” Hyde-Smith said.
findings.note: Her quote on the ATF Transparency Act, an appeal route for people wrongly denied in a gun-purchase background check.

findings.motion: ATF Transparency Act (original cosponsor; with Sen. Risch)
findings.note: Release says she is an original cosponsor of a bill to set an appeal process for people wrongly denied by the national background check and to speed National Firearms Act applications.

findings.passage: “The ATF under the Biden administration insists on issuing rules that end up infringing on the rights of law-abiding gun owners while doing next to nothing to stop violent crime.
findings.note: Her quote on the 2023 pistol brace rule; the release says she cosponsored a Congressional Review Act resolution against it and the SHORT Act.

findings.motion: Cosponsor of a Congressional Review Act resolution against the ATF pistol brace rule, and of the SHORT Act
findings.note: Release says she cosponsored both; bill numbers are not given on the page.

findings.motion: Signed letter from 30 senators urging ATF to rescind Biden-era rules
findings.note: Release lists the rules named in the letter, including the "Engaged in the Business" rule it calls a move toward universal background checks, the "Ghost Gun" rule and the pistol brace rule.

findings.motion: SHORT Act (cosponsor): removes short-barreled rifles and shotguns from the National Firearms Act
findings.note: Page, dated 2025-04-01, lists her among 11 senators who joined the bill. Bill number not given.

findings.motion: Signed Sept. 24, 2026 letter to the Attorney General asking for an investigation and destruction of ATF out-of-business dealer records
findings.note: Page names her among eight senators who signed; the letter calls the database an illegal national gun registry.

findings.passage: "Legislation that would affect the rights of American citizens under the Second Amendment should not be fast tracked by the Senate," Hyde-Smith said on the Senate floor in Washington, D.C., this morning,
findings.note: Jackson Free Press quoted her floor remarks when she objected to taking up a House-passed bill requiring background checks on all gun purchases.
